 Updated: 11:37 AM CST Nov 4, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ The Associated Press Angela Williams Digital Media Manager GREENVILLE, Miss. — Greenville residents have been told by city and Washington County officials to shelter-in-place after an explosion at a chemical plant that sent a large plume of black smoke into the air.
 Crews were notified just after 7 a.m. Wednesday of an explosion at the Loveland Products plant in Greenville, city officials said in a news release. The city in the Mississippi Delta region has a population of about 26,000 people.

No injuries were immediately reported, said Sara Moreland Hester, a deputy emergency management director for Washington County and a local firefighter. She said that as of midmorning, the fire was controlled but not fully extinguished.
 The city news release said that according to preliminary information provided by the plant management, the explosion involves a fire associated with a herbicide chemical.
 Nutrien, the parent company of Loveland, said the fire was “being managed,” and that plant leadership was working with first responders. Loveland — based in Loveland, Colorado — makes fertilizer, plant nutrition and crop protection products. 
 City officials said the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality has dispatched personnel to the area.
